questions.prompt: Which term means: the scientific name for all human beings, the only surviving human species?
questions.explanation: Homo sapiens: the scientific name for all human beings, the only surviving human species.

questions.prompt: Which term means: a group of living things with similar features that can reproduce together?
questions.explanation: Species: a group of living things with similar features that can reproduce together.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the small differences between individual members of the same species?
questions.explanation: Variation: the small differences between individual members of the same species.

questions.prompt: Which term means: variation where a feature can take any value in a range, e.g. height and weight?
questions.explanation: Continuous variation: variation where a feature can take any value in a range, e.g. height and weight.

questions.prompt: Which term means: variation where features fall into distinct separate groups, e.g. tongue rolling and eye colour?
questions.explanation: Discontinuous variation: variation where features fall into distinct separate groups, e.g. tongue rolling and eye colour.

questions.prompt: Which term means: variation gained during a lifetime from the environment or activities, not passed from parents?
questions.explanation: Acquired variation: variation gained during a lifetime from the environment or activities, not passed from parents.

questions.prompt: Which term means: a bell-shaped graph in which most values cluster near the average?
questions.explanation: Normal distribution curve: a bell-shaped graph in which most values cluster near the average.

questions.prompt: Which term means: a feature controlled by a dominant allele that appears more often in a population?
questions.explanation: Dominant characteristic: a feature controlled by a dominant allele that appears more often in a population.

questions.prompt: Which term means: a physical or behavioural feature that helps an organism survive in its environment?
questions.explanation: Adaptation: a physical or behavioural feature that helps an organism survive in its environment.

questions.prompt: Which term means: extremely cold conditions near the North Pole?
questions.explanation: Arctic conditions: extremely cold conditions near the North Pole.

questions.prompt: Which term means: a thick fat layer under the skin that provides insulation and an energy store?
questions.explanation: Blubber: a thick fat layer under the skin that provides insulation and an energy store.

questions.prompt: Which term means: blending into the surroundings to hide from predators or prey?
questions.explanation: Camouflage: blending into the surroundings to hide from predators or prey.

questions.prompt: Which term means: a material that reduces heat transfer, such as blubber and fur?
questions.explanation: Insulation: a material that reduces heat transfer, such as blubber and fur.

questions.prompt: Which term means: a waxy protective coating on a plant surface that reduces water loss?
questions.explanation: Cuticle: a waxy protective coating on a plant surface that reduces water loss.

questions.prompt: Which term means: to enter deep sleep in winter to conserve energy, with body temperature and metabolism dropping?
questions.explanation: Hibernate: to enter deep sleep in winter to conserve energy, with body temperature and metabolism dropping.

questions.prompt: Which term means: a sweet liquid in flowers that attracts insects for pollination?
questions.explanation: Nectar: a sweet liquid in flowers that attracts insects for pollination.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the transfer of pollen between flowers, needed for plant reproduction?
questions.explanation: Pollination: the transfer of pollen between flowers, needed for plant reproduction.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the process by which organisms with beneficial variations survive and reproduce more successfully?
questions.explanation: Natural selection: the process by which organisms with beneficial variations survive and reproduce more successfully.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the young produced by an organism, the next generation?
questions.explanation: Offspring: the young produced by an organism, the next generation.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the passing of characteristics from parents to offspring through genes?
questions.explanation: Heredity: the passing of characteristics from parents to offspring through genes.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the scientific study of how heredity works?
questions.explanation: Genetics: the scientific study of how heredity works.

questions.prompt: Which term means: a unit of hereditary information on a chromosome that controls one or more characteristics?
questions.explanation: Gene: a unit of hereditary information on a chromosome that controls one or more characteristics.

questions.prompt: Which term means: a thread-like structure in the cell nucleus, made of DNA, that carries many genes?
questions.explanation: Chromosome: a thread-like structure in the cell nucleus, made of DNA, that carries many genes.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the Austrian scientist (1822-1884) who founded genetics through garden pea experiments?
questions.explanation: Gregor Mendel: the Austrian scientist (1822-1884) who founded genetics through garden pea experiments.

questions.prompt: Which term means: a different form of the same gene, e.g. a black-hair allele and a blond-hair allele?
questions.explanation: Allele: a different form of the same gene, e.g. a black-hair allele and a blond-hair allele.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the more powerful allele that shows its effect even when only one copy is present?
questions.explanation: Dominant allele: the more powerful allele that shows its effect even when only one copy is present.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the weaker allele that is only expressed when two copies are present with no dominant allele?
questions.explanation: Recessive allele: the weaker allele that is only expressed when two copies are present with no dominant allele.

questions.prompt: Which term means: having two identical alleles for the same characteristic, e.g. BB or bb (also called pure bred)?
questions.explanation: Homozygous: having two identical alleles for the same characteristic, e.g. BB or bb (also called pure bred).

questions.prompt: Which term means: having two different alleles, one dominant and one recessive, e.g. Bb (also called hybrid)?
questions.explanation: Heterozygous: having two different alleles, one dominant and one recessive, e.g. Bb (also called hybrid).

questions.prompt: Which term means: the actual genetic makeup of an organism, the combination of alleles it carries?
questions.explanation: Genotype: the actual genetic makeup of an organism, the combination of alleles it carries.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the physical, observable characteristic, e.g. black hair?
questions.explanation: Phenotype: the physical, observable characteristic, e.g. black hair.

questions.prompt: Which term means: deoxyribonucleic acid, the chemical that makes up genes and chromosomes?
questions.explanation: DNA: deoxyribonucleic acid, the chemical that makes up genes and chromosomes.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the twisted-ladder shape of a DNA molecule?
questions.explanation: Double helix: the twisted-ladder shape of a DNA molecule.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the building block of DNA, made of a deoxyribose sugar, a phosphate group and an organic base?
questions.explanation: Nucleotide: the building block of DNA, made of a deoxyribose sugar, a phosphate group and an organic base.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the five-carbon sugar forming the backbone of DNA?
questions.explanation: Deoxyribose: the five-carbon sugar forming the backbone of DNA.

questions.prompt: Which term means: a chemical group forming one side of the DNA backbone?
questions.explanation: Phosphate group: a chemical group forming one side of the DNA backbone.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the sequence of A, T, C and G bases in DNA that codes for all characteristics of an organism?
questions.explanation: Genetic code: the sequence of A, T, C and G bases in DNA that codes for all characteristics of an organism.

questions.prompt: Which term means: cell division that produces two identical daughter cells, used for growth and repair?
questions.explanation: Mitosis: cell division that produces two identical daughter cells, used for growth and repair.

questions.prompt: Which term means: DNA making an exact copy of itself before cell division?
questions.explanation: Replication: DNA making an exact copy of itself before cell division.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the stage when a cell is not dividing and prepares by replicating its DNA?
questions.explanation: Interphase: the stage when a cell is not dividing and prepares by replicating its DNA.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the mitosis stage where chromosomes become visible and the nuclear membrane breaks down?
questions.explanation: Prophase: the mitosis stage where chromosomes become visible and the nuclear membrane breaks down.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the mitosis stage where the spindle forms and chromosomes line up in the middle?
questions.explanation: Metaphase: the mitosis stage where the spindle forms and chromosomes line up in the middle.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the mitosis stage where spindle fibres pull the chromatids to opposite ends?
questions.explanation: Anaphase: the mitosis stage where spindle fibres pull the chromatids to opposite ends.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the mitosis stage where nuclear membranes reform, the cytoplasm divides and two daughter cells form?
questions.explanation: Telophase: the mitosis stage where nuclear membranes reform, the cytoplasm divides and two daughter cells form.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the two identical copies of a chromosome joined together after DNA replication?
questions.explanation: Chromatids: the two identical copies of a chromosome joined together after DNA replication.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the protein-fibre structure that pulls chromosomes apart during cell division?
questions.explanation: Spindle: the protein-fibre structure that pulls chromosomes apart during cell division.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the new cells produced by division; in mitosis they are genetically identical to the parent?
questions.explanation: Daughter cells: the new cells produced by division; in mitosis they are genetically identical to the parent.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the jelly-like substance inside the cell membrane surrounding the nucleus?
questions.explanation: Cytoplasm: the jelly-like substance inside the cell membrane surrounding the nucleus.

questions.prompt: Which term means: cell division that produces four sex cells (gametes) with half the chromosome number?
questions.explanation: Meiosis: cell division that produces four sex cells (gametes) with half the chromosome number.

questions.prompt: Which term means: sex cells (egg and sperm) produced by meiosis, containing half the chromosome number?
questions.explanation: Gametes: sex cells (egg and sperm) produced by meiosis, containing half the chromosome number.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the fusion of a sperm and an egg to form a new cell (zygote)?
questions.explanation: Fertilisation: the fusion of a sperm and an egg to form a new cell (zygote).

questions.prompt: Which term means: the cell formed when sperm and egg fuse, having the full chromosome number (2n)?
questions.explanation: Zygote: the cell formed when sperm and egg fuse, having the full chromosome number (2n).

questions.prompt: Which term means: having the full chromosome number (2n), two sets, one from each parent?
questions.explanation: Diploid: having the full chromosome number (2n), two sets, one from each parent.

questions.prompt: Which term means: having half the chromosome number (n), as in gametes produced by meiosis?
questions.explanation: Haploid: having half the chromosome number (n), as in gametes produced by meiosis.

questions.prompt: Which term means: an organism genetically identical to its parent, produced by asexual reproduction (mitosis)?
questions.explanation: Clone: an organism genetically identical to its parent, produced by asexual reproduction (mitosis).

questions.prompt: Which term means: the division of cytoplasm at the end of cell division to produce two separate cells?
questions.explanation: Cytokinesis: the division of cytoplasm at the end of cell division to produce two separate cells.

questions.prompt: Which term means: a change in the genetic information (DNA sequence) of a cell?
questions.explanation: Mutation: a change in the genetic information (DNA sequence) of a cell.

questions.prompt: Which term means: a mutation affecting one gene, changing the instructions for one characteristic?
questions.explanation: Single gene mutation: a mutation affecting one gene, changing the instructions for one characteristic.

questions.prompt: Which term means: a mutation affecting the structure of one or more chromosomes, which is more severe?
questions.explanation: Chromosome mutation: a mutation affecting the structure of one or more chromosomes, which is more severe.

questions.prompt: Which term means: a mutation that gives a survival advantage and can become an adaptation through natural selection?
questions.explanation: Beneficial mutation: a mutation that gives a survival advantage and can become an adaptation through natural selection.
